header: THE FULL NAME AND THE PLACE OF A STATION, for the code the railway uses ("HWH", "KOAA", "PRRB"), so that the card can say "Howrah Junction (HWH), Howrah, West Bengal" and the reader need not decipher a code. RailRadar's answer gives each end of a train as a code and a short name ("Howrah Jn", "Kolkatta Terminal"), but no city or state, and a few names are misspelt; this table holds the stations that appear at the ends of the trains that stop at Durgapur (the 77 of 13 Nov 2026). I ALWAYS KEEP THE CODE beside the name (it is what a ticket and the railway's own boards show). Names carry no brackets of their own (the code is printed in brackets beside them). A station that is not in the table is shown by the name RailRadar gives, with no place: I guess nothing. Pratapnagar (PRTN, Vadodara, Gujarat) was added on my word (14 Nov 2026), not from a source the tool read. A JUNCTION is a station whose official name carries "Junction" (RailRadar writes "Jn"); the card marks it. I call nothing else a junction here (Agra Cantt, Malda Town and Jhajha are junctions in practice but not by name, so they are not marked).

behaviours: 77 distinct codes were seen at the ends of the trains
every one of them is in the table, Pratapnagar (PRTN) included: Vadodara, Gujarat
the table holds no code that is not a real end of those trains (no stray entries)
every entry has a full name, a city and a known state (a typo in a state would show here)
no name carries brackets of its own (the code is printed in brackets beside it)
no name is left abbreviated as 'Jn' or 'Jn.' (written out as Junction) and none keeps the railway source's misspelling 'Kolkatta'

the biggest ends read plainly: HWH Howrah Junction, Howrah, West Bengal; KOAA Kolkata Chitpur; SDAH Sealdah; NDLS New Delhi (Delhi); SMVB Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, Karnataka; CSMT Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai
the code always comes back with the name, and the table's name wins over the railway source's
a station that is not in the table keeps the name the source gave and has no place (nothing is guessed)
Pratapnagar reads: Pratapnagar (PRTN), Vadodara, Gujarat, and is not a junction
a junction is a station whose name says Junction: Howrah, Asansol, Jabalpur, Patna are; Sealdah, Durgapur, Delhi, Shalimar, Surat are not
a station not in the table is a junction when the source's name says Jn or Junction, and not otherwise
Durgapur and its neighbours are right: DGR Durgapur, UDL Andal Junction, ASN Asansol Junction, BWN Bardhaman Junction, all West Bengal
